processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting followed by vacuum arc remelting (VIM + VAR)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: VIM + VAR used to obtain 500 kg ingots of the 0Al steel.
Ingots forged into billets of Φ170 mm; characterization specimens extracted from the quarter-radius position.
Solution treatment performed to dissolve carbides, applied identically to the 0Al and 1.3Al steels.
Water quenching after solution treatment; the resulting as-quenched sample of the 0Al steel is denoted 0Al,WQ (before tempering).

structures.overall_structure: As-quenched martensitic structure of the low alloy ultrahigh strength 0Al steel (martensitic matrix); the paper reports detailed microstructural quantification for the tempered condition rather than the WQ state.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile: diameter 5 mm, gauge length 25 mm; Charpy U-notch impact: 10 × 10 × 55 mm3
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Three tests per sample condition were performed; impact specimen surfaces and notches were mechanically polished.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of 0Al,WQ (Fig. 1a): rises steeply above the 2000 MPa gridline, peaks at ~2300 MPa (UTS 2294 ± 9 MPa) between engineering strain ~8 and ~9, then falls to ~2100 MPa at ~10% strain.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; strain rate 0.001 s^-1; specimens of 5 mm diameter and 25 mm gauge length; three tests per sample condition.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the as-quenched yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and total elongation of the 0Al steel (0Al,WQ).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens 10 × 10 × 55 mm3; surfaces and notches mechanically polished; three tests per sample condition.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the impact absorption energy (KU2) of the 0Al steel in the as-quenched condition.

unmapped_findings: Impact absorption energy (Charpy U-notch, KU2) of 0Al,WQ = 33 ± 6 J (Fig. 1b and Table 2); the schema provides no dedicated slot for impact absorption energy.
Fracture toughness KIC was not measured for the as-quenched 0Al,WQ condition (shown as a dash in Table 2); KIC is only reported for the tempered 0Al,2h condition (97.6 MPa·m^1/2).
Matrix composition of the 0Al steel (mass fraction, wt%, Table 1): C 0.32, Si 1.98, Mn 1.02, Cr 1.00, Ni 3.41, Mo 0.56, V 0.09, Al 0.03.
Specimens for microstructural and mechanical characterization of the 0Al steel were extracted from the quarter-radius position of the Φ170 mm forged billet.

In the as-quenched (WQ) state the 0Al reference steel is stronger and tougher than the 1.3Al steel: 0Al,WQ YS 1234 ± 22 MPa, UTS 2294 ± 9 MPa, TE 9.5 ± 0.6 %, KU2 33 ± 6 J versus 1.3Al,WQ YS 1113 ± 11 MPa, UTS 2145 ± 144 MPa, TE 4.3 ± 0.9 %, KU2 23 ± 2 J; the 1.3Al steel fractured before reaching its maximum tensile strength.

The 0Al,WQ sample is the as-quenched baseline/reference condition of the 0Al steel prior to the 180 °C / 2 h tempering that produces the 0Al,2h condition (the tempered condition carries the retained austenite, dislocation-density and NiAl-cluster data).
